original: Look at the calculation.
Trading, services, small crafts...
There's nobody anymore who wants to work in a good old manufactory.
This might surprise you, but... I have plenty of workers willing to work at my factory.
At least, I hope they're willing... It's better than what they'd be doing otherwise.
Your factory? With conveyor belts and automated workbenches?
Yeah... a real underground facility...
Oh, I'd love to see that!
Now that you're so excited, I feel like I should meet certain expectations...
As soon as I check everything over, I'll gladly invite you for a tour.
The second problem?
So, what's this calculation were you talking about?
What's the second problem?
The steel quality...
We'll never achieve the finest quality steel from the Royal Foundry.
Maybe we can restore it?
We might not need to.. Some days ago, I saw smoke coming out of it.
We just need someone to reach it, and check whether the iron masters are still producing steel.
Lucky for you... I'm already working on that.
Is it far? How do we get there?
It's on the north side of the town.
The only way to reach it is through a water tunnel.
Luckily, I know all about it.
I'll bring you some samples, and you can check the quality.
That would be great.
Just great... meanwhile, I still have 25 years of work ahead of me...
It's my industrialization plan.
See these numbers... even with all the resources I have, it'll take 25 years to reach pre-apocalypse levels.
And that was only supposed to be the beginning...
I see... so what's the problem, now that your resources are covered?
There's two main problems.
I'm all alone here... Even if I built a factory, there'd be no one to work in it...
They barely escaped death, but they're all too refined for hard work.
Front-of-the-Envelope Calculation
Tales for Ales
Here’s your beer.
One great story later...
That was a great story! You said you had more?
Yeah... but now I’m sad... and not in the mood for another one.
All my stories are in the past... and as for what's awaiting me... well, I already have gray hair.
Maybe another beer will cheer you up.
Nah... I'll need something stronger than beer... if I'm gonna believe I still have any decent stories ahead.
Ah, good... you know, I’ve seen you before.
Another tavern — the Dead Horse.
I thought we’d end up on some grand adventure together... but no.
Then I saw you again... It felt like a sign. Have you any adventures to share?
Honestly, I can’t think of any right now.
I see... you know, I consider myself quite a remarkable character...
Maybe next time.
Maybe... alright then, story time!
Give faith.
Trust me... you have adventures still ahead of you. Just give it time.
... You know what? I believe you. Want to hear another story?
Heh... telling these stories just makes me sad...
Hey... want to hear one of my stories?
Are they any good?
Only the best. I used to be a captain... until my ship sank.
Buy me a beer and I’ll prove it.
High-quality steel.
But there aren't any masters left there.
Then who forged this steel?
A group of monks live there now. They run the foundry.
Monks... mastering steel and producing this?
Apparently, yes.
But that's unbelievable! How could they? It would take years...
By the way, I cleared the way to the foundry. We can trade with them now.
Good news... but still — how did they do it? Even I couldn't master the process.
No idea. They just work together. Calmly.
I see... together...
Jack, I brought an ingot from the Royal Foundry.
Thanks.
See if it's still any good.
Let me check...
There's a simple test for that.
Oh my...
Is that bad?
No... quite the opposite. It's better than ever.
It looks like the iron masters finally perfected their craft.
Show my factory.
They never get tired.
And no toilet breaks either, I bet...
Did you really build all of this?
Mostly. The space and the underfloor belt gears were already here.
I just repaired and connected them.
And this is under the Inquisitor's base, right?
That's right.
That explains everything.
The king used this place to produce goods for the entire town.
It was so cheap, the guilds could barely compete.
I have something I think might impress you.
He had a perfect monopoly. Prisoners probably did all the work.
Well... I'm glad everything is in good hands now.
It's incredible you achieved all this so quickly...
You're meeting the entire town's demands...
You've surpassed everything I ever imagined.
Let's go back... to my... humble shack...
You mean your underground factory?
Exactly. I think I'm ready to show it.
This is my modern production line.
Unbelievable... it's bigger than anything I've ever seen.
Conveyor belts everywhere... but where does all the power come from?
You see those guys running, turning the wheels?
Yes... I see them.
Factory Tour
The best armor.
I'll keep them safe. If things go bad again, they'll earn the right to wear them.
You're a cautious man.
Life taught me to be. I never had things easy, so I learned to prepare for the worst.
I'm tired, Keeper... and not the kind of tired that a good sleep can fix.
I think you've done enough. You've earned a peaceful life.
Yeah... I think I am ready to retire. Now it's your problem... Ha ha.
Agatha offered me a corner in her place. My first real home in my life... I've always lived in the barracks.
Strange how a crossroads can become so peaceful.
I'll find myself a little place nearby. I'd like to live closer to Agatha.
Thank you, Keeper. Truly.
Good thing I pack light. My sword, my memories... my new armor... and that's about it.
This armor is a true masterpiece... exactly what you asked for.
Ha... Every master brags about his creations...
But this one really deserves it. It's incredible. Better than the King's Guard used to wear.
One for you. The rest for your lads.
Mine goes on display. The others I'll keep oiled and carefully stored.
I thought you were going to give them to your guards.
Oh, they're safe for now... all thanks to you.
Those lazy fools would just scratch them on the tavern benches, or pawn them for ale.
Not in Shining Armor Yet
Let us pray for good steel, brothers!
You're eight years older now... and your eyes give you away.
What do they say?
Yours challenge the world. His only endured it.
I see you know a lot. And that's good.
I have expected this day. I've prepared my answers.
The other me.
Can you tell me about the other version of me?
Was he a villain who destroyed the world?
He was... and still is... my friend.
He wanted to fix things. It all just ended in the usual way.
Amen.
So... was the zombie apocalypse his fault?
I hope not... Honestly I don't know how it could be done without portal magic.
We removed it from the palace — the portal and all its magic.
Why move it?
We all began abusing it for our own benefit.
But in our defense, it was the Keeper's wife who started it.
She always wanted more. Power. A crown. Nonsense.
So six of us activated the portal, and stole it away from the Royal Palace.
After that... everything fell apart.
I only hope it wasn't because of us.
Your Highness!
I told you not to call me that... please.
Dear me... and who is this? A new Graveyard Keeper.
Familiar, yet entirely different. Ha ha...
Please continue the service without me, brothers.
How did you realize I'm not the same Keeper?
Ha ha... a fair question.
Use the magic mirror.
To get the portal piece...
Hm... what should I ask for... I don't actually need anything personally...
Then maybe you can just give me the portal piece?
No, no... ha ha... that's not how things work here. Let's see...
My brothers are tired of pumping the bellows by hand.
I can send you some zombies...
Oh, we don't need whole zombies here...
Alright, I’ll bring you just zombie power.
I'm not sure, but it might work.
Ha ha... I haven't given anyone a quest in eight years...
Let's try that mirror.
As you wish. It's quite simple.
Mirror... mirror... show me the first part of the magic portal.
You are the most beautiful, of course... wait... what? The portal part... give me a second.
Very funny... it's right behind you!
Very funny indeed. Ha ha...
So I can take the first piece and use the mirror to find the others?
Of course. But first, you'll need to do my quests.
Magic Mirror
The Magic Portal
My wife?
Yes. Your other self brought her here. That was a mistake.
The mirror can reveal the location of the next portal fragment.
The magic is a little fancy, so for the first time... we'll use it together.
I need to find the magic portal and use it to save the world.
My brother and I stole it from the Palace... from your other self.
Your wife wished to become a queen, moved into the Palace, and took the portal with her.
We split it up, so they couldn't recover it and use it again.
Interesting... and where are the pieces now?
That's a very good question. I scattered seven pieces among different people.
No easy way this time...
Fortunately, I took a magic mirror from your wife.
Quest for the mirror
Vagner? Hmm... you mean the astrologer, Gunter?
Call him whatever you like. I think you know who I mean.
That mirror is kind of rude.
It's had a tough life...
So... what's the second quest?
You know what? You seem like a decent fellow.
One quest will be enough.
Thank you, I guess... So can I have the mirror?
Sure... but could you try it here to find the next piece... just to make sure it works.
Alright.
Mirror... mirror... show me the second portal fragment.
The second piece lies in the home of your friend... the poet, Vagner.
Man of Steel
High-quality steel.
Ha ha... not quite. We've also studied every metallurgy book we could find.
I see. So can I get some of that steel?
Of course. Ha ha. It is for sale.
Hey, I see the smelting furnace is still working.
Indeed it is. First it boiled the water for our baths, and now it smelts the finest steel.
So you're still making high-quality steel?
We certainly hope so.
But how? And why? You're monks... you're supposed to make wine at the very most.
It's part of our vow of obedience.
We gather around the furnace and pray to its spirit.
That's all?
PR campaign target.
I could command all the attention I once craved... but I didn't need it then.
I think you're trying to say that friendship is more important than public approval.
Well said... And now it's time to help my friend Jack.
So what's this grand project?
Patience. Jack has to approve it first.
Plus, a project of this scale deserves a proper announcement.
About Jack... I believe he'll agree to join you.
That's great. I'll talk to him. We'll make this project right here at the port!
Heh... I think Jack is still refusing to let go of his factory.
But I'll show him I can handle the Town's production needs myself.
Sure... just be gentle with him. He tries to look tougher than he is.
In the meantime, I'll get everything ready. We'll launch the project at the port.
We've reached our target.
Excellent. I knew we were on the correct trajectory.
That's another role I've perfected!
Poet. Magical Beast. Astrologer. And now — PR strategist.
You perfected the Magic Beast role?
Yeeeh... it was a brief, but very dramatic part of my life.
I might have liked that role the most... I was part of something big. Just like now.
Surrounded by friends. Supported. Confident.
Why don't you like me?
Piece of a portal
I don't know what they wished for last time... but now the day of the week are a total mess.
And apparently, I'm the only one who notices... the Astrologer.
Ok, maybe the days will get back to normal after we fix the world.
Fine... Perhaps fixing time itself is part of saving the world.
Mirror... mirror... reveal the third portal fragment.
Interesting... Would you care to explain, or shall I?
You want to tell him yourself?
You see... I once had two fragments. Charm gave me hers.
But I wasn't always a respected PR manager and astrologer.
Back then, I needed the money... so I sold it.
I know you have the second pice of the portal. Mirrors don't lie.
You did what? To whom?
In my defense, I got an excellent price... even for a magical relic.
Where it is now?
Somewhere in the middle of the sea.
It left on a merchant ship.
Unbelievable...
Relax. We can buy it back. Everything is negotiable. Speak to the Trade Master at the Main Pier.
I sure hope so.
After all, what kind of story would this be if the hero couldn't fix his mistakes?
It was your mistake!
Ah, so you visited Brother Bishop... he used to be quite the man of fashion, you know.
You have a point. Now go and talk with the Trade Master.
Back then, he had presence.
So, Gunter... or should I say Vagner — where's the fragment?
It's here. I always hoped someone would come and restore the portal.
If the Bishop trusted you with the mirror, I suppose I can trust you too.
I just hope you'll ask about fixing the days of the week.
What's wrong with the days?
The Hungry Cosmos
The church quality.
Yes. Kind. To people. Ridiculous of course.
It's actually a good thing to be kind to others.
Oh, how fortunate for me... so, Mr. Kindness. I think I'll ask you for some help.
I'm ready. Especially if it proves I'm right.
It's... delicate. I need to choose my words carefully.
I did what I could. The church looks magnificent.
For once... I don't feel like shouting at you.
Those readings are bringing out my soft side...
And I might even enjoy it.
That's not a bad thing, you know.
Herbert says the same thing...
He says I should be... what was it... ki... kin...
Kind?
See You in Church
Then maybe you should go find it yourself?
The sewer is gigantic... we'll need more clues to find the place...
Where did this cheese come from?
Hm...
Hey, it's from Mauritzio's cheese factory... Rivers surround it on three sides.
It used to be the best aged cheese in town.
Yeah, good cheese... a gift from the gods... ha ha.
If only we could reach his cellar where he kept it...
Wait a minute! Maybe the Ancient God is there...
The Old God? Anyway, if you help my guys get into the cellars...
Then half the cheese is yours... and the Ancient God too, of course... ha ha.
Oh, I will... cough-cough
Let's go, guys. Drinks on me!
Is that the god who can cure my sister?
I think so... are you starting to believe?
Cheese just appearing out of nowhere... cough-cough
Yes... perhaps... and it might well be my last chance... my cough is growing worse...
I'm really sorry, Albert.
Promise me... if I'm gone, will you ask him about Aleksta?
I promise.
I trust you.
Maybe there's something we can do for your health?
Hey! Don't talk to the customers that way!
There may be a way... but I'm to busy to research it.
Uh... you mind if I take this cheese, by the way?
Ask for hints.
Sorry to interrupt you guys.
Tell him... that the price is ridiculous...
It's a dangerous job...
I need to find a place in the sewer...
A cell, but not for humans...
Finding Old God
Looking for someone, sweetheart?
You know where Davy the Dagger is?
He's near the sewer entrance, by the west gate...
Dealing with some work-related issues.
Thanks.
Ding dong. Bing bang bong. Dig I am! Or am I?
Long story.
Very long story.
Anyway, I've come here to see you, Keeper Two.
Right now you're the one shaping this story... and shaping the whole world with it.
So I brought you a little gift. Something that lets you see what isn't there.
Your destiny is to take this Red Eye — a fragment of an ancient god's power.
An ancient god... seeing what isn't there... hmm.
Could it help me find a door in a solid wall?
A door? Possibly. But tools like this require... imagination.
Right... because I need that door to free an ancient god. I'd like to talk to him.
What? Who the sard are you?
If I were you... I wouldn't.
Ancient God
Why shouldn't I talk to him?
He seems caring. A good guy, your buddy the ancient god.
He treats the world like it's a play written purely for his own entertainment.
Sometimes he helps the actors. Sometimes he replaces them.
Sometimes he just enjoys watching them suffer. He's dangerous.
How do you know so much about him?
He was the god's High Priest and prophet... am I right?
I was...
Nice to meet you, Keeper Two.
Also... there were some golden apples once. Apples that grant absolute wisdom.
Long story short... I ate two of them.
Red eye
Hmm... how did you get this Red Eye from the god?
Ha... I was just in the right place at the right time. Picked it up off the floor, literally.
Your wife... the Keeper's wife... wished for it with the portal.
But she had no use for it. She wasn't the right type. She wasn't a Keeper.
You, however... You could reshape the world with it.
So I can skip restoring the portal to save the world?
The portal is the core mechanic... I mean... the central power of this world.
How did you get in here? I locked the door.
But I had a feeling you'd need the eye to keep the story moving.
What about the other keepers?
If you really do have endless wisdom, I have a lot of questions.
Too many answers bring too much pain. I've been there.
Besides, I need to catch a ship and leave Town.
When this story ends, I want to be very far away.
Alright then... give me the eye.
How am I supposed to use it?
I thought that guy must have lost his mind after eating those apples.
So... how exactly do you know him, my friend?
Someone must've left it open. These things happen.
Don't start... that's a totally different story from a very long time ago.
Believe me, you wouldn't enjoy hearing it. It would take forever.
Besides, you can probably read about it in some dusty library.
Alright then... If I want any answers, I guess I'll have to go to the sewers and find that door.
Donkey said he saw someone heading this way...
Well hello, Lucius. You've lost some weight I see. Ha ha.
Digus... good to see you! Though I go by Larry now.
Hold on. You two know each other?
Friend or Foe
Wealthy townspeople
I did as you asked. The shops are packed with lavish, unnecessary items.
I've already seen a surge of wealthy patrons at the club.
Well done. You're a hero... to me and to the town. Ha ha...
Now we just have to cure Albert's cough.
I can't have him frightening away my best customers!
After we cure him... with my gentle touch, he can become a very respectable doctor.
I was frozen with fear... Aleksta was the one who saved us.
That day I swore I'd become beautiful and brave.
And you have.
But it didn't bring me happiness.
Only after meeting Albert have I come to understand. I could truly be happy with him.
He's different... thoughtful... passionate...
Yes, he's quite a character.
I want to thank you... for everything you've done.
I'll be so happy to be near him...
Is there anything else I can do for you?
It's the least I can do for him.
You've done enough. I'll speak to Albert myself.
I don't think you owe Albert anything.
Well... yes and no. I was friends with Aleksta. She was so beautiful.
Everyone adored her. I was just the awkward little duckling.
Ha... it's hard to believe that now.
Now I know how to carry myself... how to be admired...
But back then, I was just jealous.
We were together when the zombies came.
Wealthy Clients
At last... I was starting to worry it would take you forever.
Actual zombie hordes?
Yes. They captured the entire Town. We only recently starting pushing them back.
Wow... that Keeper sounds like a disaster.
Did he and his beloved still have the portal?
No. It was split into fragments. I'm trying to collect them all.
Hmm... Breaking the portal might be a really bad idea.
I need you to tell me how to use the portal properly, so I can wish the world back to normal.
My sister is always being so dramatic. Every couple of years, someone "ruins the world"...
Yet here we all are, still standing.
On the other hand, starting fresh somewhere else wouldn't be so bad...
I was even a little worried I'd run out of cheese to guide you.
I don't like what I'm hearing. I'll give you your eye back, but only if you help me.
Ah, these Keepers and their free will...
How to use the portal
I need to know how to use the portal and make the right wish.
Well, obviously you need the complete portal... all seven stones.
To activate it, the seven passions... or sins... must stand near it.
I thought I only needed to collect the fragments. Where do I find the people?
I wouldn't want to brag, but in my prime, I could activate the portal all by myself.
So you could activate it for me?
Not anymore. Being a god sounds impressive, but it drains your passion.
To be honest, the cheese didn't guide me much... it was mostly just frustrating.
Then maybe I could do it myself...
No. I deliberately choose Keepers without all seven passions. No offense.
None taken. Then how do I activate the portal?
You must find seven people, one for each day of the week.
But there's only six days here.
Yes, I know... six looks better on the wheel of time.
So you need six people.
And how do I find them?
You probably already have. Or they found you. You'll feel they're special somehow.
Your connection with them will become clearer.
You're right... but with such little power left, the cheese hints were the best I could manage.
Earn their full trust... one hundred percent of it.... and bring them to the portal.
That's it?
Yes, that's it. Now my eye, please. I am a god after all.
With my eye, the portal can work even if you gain only ninety percent of their trust. This will save you some time.
Anyway... I feel that you have my eye. Give it back now, so you can finish this story.
I'll regain my power, and you can remain a Keeper for another... let me see... forty years!
Wait a minute... I think it's my destiny to save the world.
According to who?
The fairy, and your sister. They said the other me, Keeper One, ruined the world and awakened the zombie hordes. And the world might die soon.
I have some questions first.
Oh really? One of those Keepers who wants to know everything...
Or we could just skip that part, and go straight to saving the world.
I have some questions first.
I'll gladly answer them after you return my eye.
How did you become a god?
That happened many years ago... When I was young. Younger than you, actually.
I loved reading history and fantasy books.
I was a dreamer... and through those dreams, and a bit of bad luck, my sister and I ended up here.
There was nothing here but a portal in the void.
It seemed ready to grant our wishes. So I created this world.
I never asked to become a god... but I suppose this is how you become one.
Tell me about portal.
There's not much I can tell. It was already here when I arrived.
It grants wishes when activated.
Though it tends to twist them in rather awkward ways.
Your sister
She is... or was... a wonderful girl. She loved nature and animals.
While I was building my little empire, she spent her time with the trees and the rabbits.
I met her. She seems a bit lost now.
Truth is, there's not much excitement in simply observing nature.
After losing oneself in it for so many years... of course one can become a little strange.
Keepers and the old contract
At some point I grew bored with this place.
I decided to travel to other worlds for a while, just to see what things were like elsewhere.
So I came up with a clever plot twist.
The idea was, I'd leave someone from the real world here in my place.
Someone with free will, to keep things running.
A new god... a Keeper. You were all just meant to be my temporary replacements.
But somehow, all of you managed to disappoint me. Too much free will.
Not you though. You're a decent Keeper.
What powers do you have.
Oh, all the usual divine powers... lightning bolts, thunder, dramatic entrances... ha ha.
Just kidding. My real power is my imagination.
Making things up.
And my eye helps me see interesting ways to bring those things to life.
I used to believe in my own power...
But now I rely on other people's faith in me.
Why do you need the red eye?
I told you... It helps me. It reveals what is hidden.
It brings ideas to the surface.
But it also gives you magical power, right?
Not exactly... it's more like a curse.
But I found a way to control it... and even enjoy it.
How did you lose your eye?
Someone not very bright decided to punish me, using the power of the portal.
But instead he only cursed himself.
Though to be honest, being locked up with all that cheese was not very pleasant.
So I suppose I was punished after all.
Give the eye
Alright. A deal is a deal. Here's your eye. But I still need your help.
Of course. I'm a good god, after all... though I have but little power left.
I require some faith. Please perform my ritual.
That wasn't part of the deal.
It will be much faster than earning that last ten percent of trust.
So... complete the portal, gain the trust of six people, and perform the ritual.
In any order... but I suggest you hurry with the ritual. Then I can help you with those six.
Farewell... I have some godly business to attend to.
I have some questions first.
I have things to do, and you must perform a ceremony for me.
Let's focus on that. I'll answer your questions afterward. I promise.
See you after the ceremony.
Keep the red eye.
I could repair the attic in my house. Would that suit you?
Ha ha... a fine place for a powerless god.
Let me know when it's ready.
That's quite a lot to process.
While I'm fixing the portal and thinking all this through, I'd better hold on to the eye.
Oh Keeper, don't make me regret this.
You'll get it back once I save the world.
A poor decision indeed... but I suppose free will is free will.
Still, I cannot remain here any longer, surrounded by mountains of cheese.
I'm not really sure where you could stay...
Well, I could stay at your place for a while.
Impressive... just like in the old days. They built this temple to earn my forgiveness.
And I am. I'm quietly removing their last doubts. But the final step is yours.
Those six
I have some questions.
You know, I once knew a man who went mad from having too many answers.
I like you, and I don't want to see you go mad... So you can ask two questions.
But they forgot — not everything is about walls.
Did you regain enough power?
Yes. I regained it even before the ceremony. Your own belief in me was enough.
Still... I must admit, the ceremony was rather pleasant.
I'm glad you liked it. Now tell me more about those six people.
Simple. Just go to them, and ask for their help activating the magic portal.
You might offer them a wish from the portal as payment. That usually works.
You said you'd help me convince them.
Eye, Red Eye
Love Story
Hey Albert. It's nice to see you moved into a proper house.
He's doing a lot... even helping me run the Club.
Linda deserves some help. A beautiful girl like her shouldn't have to work all day.
You're very sweet, Albert.
I'm glad you two met. Maybe there's something I can do for you.
Actually, yes. I've run out of bottles for my medicine.
The demand is enormous these days. Could you craft some for me? Something... appropriately professional.
Oh, poor girl... let me help.
Maybe Linda also needs something?
Oh, I think she's doing fine.
Alright, I need to get back to my patients. I'll see you later with the bottles.
Yes... Linda can be very persuasive.
Bye, Albert.
Keeper, wait a moment.
I heard you asking how you could help us.
That's right.
Could you bring me some chocolate? I heard it's quite special.
The merchants recently brought some cocoa seeds.
Sure, I'll see what I can do.
If only. He built a laboratory in the basement, and spends all his time down there.
But I also opened a small office on the second floor for patients.
I'm only teasing. I can see you're really trying to change... and I respect that.
Hold on... Albert, is that your sister working behind the bar?
Yes, that's Aleksta. We taught her how to serve beer.
Linda and I thought it might help with her recovery.
But I'm still doing my experiments. Of course between Linda and all the clients, I don't have as much time.
Behold! I sensed my new residence was ready, so I arrived.
No, I don't. Now that you have a place to stay, tell me more about those six people.
You just need to ask them for a favor... to help you activate the magic portal.
You can bribe them with promises of portal wishes.
That sounds like a decent plan.
Exactly. Repair the portal, convince the six... and don't forget to invite me!
After all, you'll still need me to perform a small trick before you can make proper wishes.
Naturally... you wouldn't want us doing it all without you.
The six
Can you tell me who those six are?
You really don't know? I thought you were an experienced Keeper.
Psst... I saw him hiding in a nearby bush for quite some time.
I just want to be sure.
Yes, yes... better safe than sorry. Six sins ... six people.
Linda, the owner of the Dockside Club. Albert the doctor.
Agatha the nun. Herbert the guard.
Gunter the... PR manager. And Jack the craftsman.
But there are seven stones... who activates the last one?
As far as I know, that always happens rather mysteriously. Someone appears at the last moment.
I suppose it's meant to teach a valuable lesson.
Well... you are a god after all.
Yes, a god living in your attic.
Follow me, I'll show you to your attic.
So, how's our ancient god doing?
You know... he actually seems like a reasonably nice guy.
Still, it's strange having a god living in your attic.
A talking skull is strange too, but I got used to it.

bg: Направи мое копие... или ме раздели на две...

original: And then I found myself at the Inquisitor’s headquarters.
bg: И тогава се озовах в щаба на инквизитора.

original: You know the rest...
bg: Знаеш останалото...

original: The sad part is, I couldn’t die there... But it was still very painful...
bg: Тъжното е, че не можех да умра там... Но пак беше много болезнено...

original: So maybe I lost some part of my mind...
bg: Така че може би съм загубил част от разума си...

original: Don’t be scared. You’re with Larry now.
bg: Не се страхувай. Сега си с Лари.

original: Go to sleep.
bg: Лягай да спиш.

original: So, how is everything around here?
bg: И така, как вървят нещата тук?

original: Fresh air, hard work... I kind of enjoy it.
bg: Свеж въздух, усилена работа... Май ми харесва.

original: Good... I took a risk and snooped around the base.
bg: Добре... Поех риск и порових из базата.

original: Surprisingly, there's notes scattered all over the place.
bg: Изненадващо, навсякъде са разхвърляни записки.

original: A lot of them... no idea who wrote them, or why.
bg: И то много... Нямам представа кой ги е писал и защо.

original: What kind of notes? Anything useful?
bg: Какви записки? Нещо полезно?

original: Mostly words. Emotions. Stuff like that... I read them.
bg: Предимно думи. Емоции. Такива неща... Прочетох ги.

original: So you wouldn’t have to.
bg: За да не се налага на теб.

original: That’s what I learned about the last days before the apocalypse.
bg: Това научих за последните дни преди апокалипсиса.

original: It all started about eight years ago.
bg: Всичко започна преди около осем години.

original: Then one day, even the living started turning undead. In masses.
bg: После един ден дори живите започнаха да се превръщат в немъртви. Масово.

original: It began near the Royal Palace, and soon swallowed up most of the town.
bg: Започна край Кралския дворец и скоро погълна по-голямата част от града.

original: They'd been having trouble with their dead long before that...
bg: Много преди това вече имаха проблеми с мъртвите си...

original: Something about betraying their gods. Twice.
bg: Нещо за това, че са предали боговете си. Два пъти.

original: But that's not important.
bg: Но това не е важно.

original: Everything really went downhill after a strange man who couldn’t die appeared...
bg: Всичко наистина тръгна надолу, след като се появи странен човек, който не можеше да умре...

original: A man who was meant to be you.
bg: Човек, който е трябвало да бъдеш ти.

original: After that, the dead began to rise...
bg: След това мъртвите започнаха да се надигат...

original: Before anyone could bury them in the northern graveyard...
bg: Преди някой да успее да ги погребе в северното гробище...

original: Or send them off on ships.
bg: Или да ги изпрати по море.

original: Then the zombie transformations just stopped...
bg: После превръщанията в зомбита просто спряха...

original: But there were already too many undead...
bg: Но немъртвите вече бяха прекалено много...

original: Now people fear every dead body...
bg: Сега хората се страхуват от всяко мъртво тяло...

original: Yet somehow they’ve learned to live in this mess.
bg: И все пак някак са се научили да живеят в тази бъркотия.

original: Very interesting...
bg: Много интересно...

original: I’ve got an update about your situation.
bg: Имам новини за положението ти.

original: Remember when you told me about the guy with red eyes who split you in half...
bg: Помниш ли как ми разказа за човека с червените очи, който те раздели на две...

original: You found some more notes somewhere...
bg: Намерил си още записки някъде...

original: Yeah... mostly about the final day of a guy named Rufus.
bg: Да... предимно за последния ден на един човек на име Руфъс.

original: Personal stuff. You know how it is...
bg: Лични неща. Знаеш как е...

original: Plus I have another trusted source...
bg: Освен това имам още един надежден източник...

original: Someone big in the grave business.
bg: Някой важен в гробарския бизнес.

original: Someone with long ears?
bg: Някой с дълги уши?

original: Yep... a certain donkey, very talkative. Full of strange theories.
bg: Да... едно магаре, което обича да говори. Пълно е със странни теории.

original: I’m listening...
bg: Слушам те...

original: The man with red eyes was once a local god.
bg: Човекът с червените очи някога е бил местен бог.

original: Long story short... the Old God showed the people mercy, and signed a contract with them.
bg: Накратко... Старият бог се смилил над хората и сключил договор с тях.

original: He gave them a Graveyard Keeper to guide their souls and grant them peace after death.
bg: Дал им Гробар, който да напътства душите им и да им осигурява покой след смъртта.

original: There were many graveyard keepers, each serving their time...
bg: Имало е много гробари, всеки от които служел за своето време...

original: Each brought here from distant lands.
bg: Всеки доведен тук от далечни земи.

original: And just when you appeared, another one arrived in the North Graveyard.
bg: И точно когато ти се появи, друг пристигна в Северното гробище.

original: He looks exactly like you...
bg: Той изглежда точно като теб...

original: He provided people everything, in exchange for worshiping him.
bg: Той осигурявал на хората всичко в замяна на тяхното поклонение.

original: Then they betrayed him... for a newer god.
bg: После го предали... заради един по-нов бог.

original: After that, they were on their own with all their problems and their needs.
bg: След това останали сами с всичките си проблеми и нужди.

original: They abandoned all the old rituals, and the cycle of reincarnation collapsed.
bg: Изоставили всички стари ритуали и цикълът на прераждането се сринал.

original: The lost souls became a real problem...
bg: Изгубените души се превърнали в истински проблем...

original: What about the second god, and the second betrayal you mentioned?
bg: Ами вторият бог и второто предателство, за които спомена?

original: Not important. The second god was a failure.
bg: Не е важно. Вторият бог беше провал.

original: Now stop interrupting...
bg: А сега спри да ме прекъсваш...

original: But something bad happened to him...
bg: Но нещо лошо му се случило...

original: And I believe you’re the new Graveyard Keeper now.
bg: И вярвам, че сега ти си новият Гробар.

original: Hm... no one ever told me any of that. I’m not sure...
bg: Хм... никой никога не ми е разказвал нищо от това. Не съм сигурен...

original: Then tell me... doesn’t it seem odd to you, that a certificate appears when you bury a body?
bg: Тогава ми кажи... не ти ли се струва странно, че при погребване на тяло се появява свидетелство?

original: Now that you mention it... yeah, that is a little strange.
bg: Като го спомена... да, това е малко странно.

original: Exactly. It’s part of an ancient contract...
bg: Точно така. То е част от древен договор...

original: And you’re part of it too now.
bg: А сега и ти си част от него.

original: Comrade Donkey
bg: Другарю Магаре

original: I think I can find out more about the other keeper... the one who might be you.
bg: Мисля, че мога да разбера повече за другия гробар... онзи, който може да си ти.

original: That’s good news. I can’t believe any part of me could be that bad.
bg: Това е добра новина. Не мога да повярвам, че някоя част от мен може да е била толкова лоша.

original: There’s just one problem... I'll need beer.
bg: Има само един проблем... ще ми трябва бира.

original: Can you even drink?
bg: Ти изобщо можеш ли да пиеш?

original: Not for me. For our comrade... the donkey.
bg: Не за мен. За нашия другар... магарето.

original: Someone taught the poor beast how to drink.
bg: Някой е научил горкото животно да пие.

original: Alright. I’ll bring some if it helps loosen his tongue.
bg: Добре. Ще донеса, ако това помогне да му развърже езика.

original: Donkey has never seen him since...
bg: Оттогава Магарето не го е виждало...

original: Never mind.
bg: Няма значение.

original: Maybe his wish came true, and he went home.
bg: Може би желанието му се е сбъднало и се е прибрал у дома.

original: Maybe...
bg: Може би...

original: Hey, don't you want to go back too?
bg: Хей, и ти ли не искаш да се върнеш?

original: No... not really. Sure there's things I miss...
bg: Не... не особено. Разбира се, има неща, които ми липсват...

original: But I think I belong here now.
bg: Но мисля, че сега мястото ми е тук.

original: Were you "where you belonged" chained up in the dungeon? Ha.
bg: Мястото ти ли беше в тъмницата, окован? Ха.

original: Yeah... maybe it’s Stockholm syndrome.
bg: Да... може би е стокхолмски синдром.

original: What syndrome?
bg: Какъв синдром?

original: Now I’m almost certain the other keeper was you...
bg: Сега съм почти сигурен, че другият гробар си бил ти...

original: He was a decent enough fellow. A little greedy.
bg: Беше що-годе свестен човек. Малко алчен.

original: Not exactly respectful to corpses...
bg: Не се отнасяше особено почтително към труповете...

original: But overall, not a bad guy.
bg: Но като цяло не беше лош човек.

original: Always dreaming of going back to his world...
bg: Винаги мечтаеше да се върне в своя свят...

original: He discovered a legend about a wish-granting portal...
bg: Открил легенда за портал, който изпълнява желания...

original: And put all his energy into restoring it...
bg: И вложил всичките си сили във възстановяването му...

original: He thought he'd fixed everything, with some help from his new friends.
bg: Мислел, че е оправил всичко с малко помощ от новите си приятели.

original: But then, a short time after, the undead plague began...
bg: Но малко след това започнала чумата на немъртвите...

original: Give the beer.
bg: Дай бирата.

original: Alright, wish me luck...
bg: Добре, пожелай ми късмет...

original: He’s way too excited about drinking with a skull.
bg: Прекалено се вълнува, че ще пие с череп.

original: You know, we kind of had a good time...
bg: Знаеш ли, прекарахме си доста добре...

original: He even gave me a ride on his back...
bg: Дори ме повози на гърба си...

original: So, did you learn anything useful?
bg: И така, научи ли нещо полезно?

original: Eh... more than enough...
bg: Ех... повече от достатъчно...

original: Fish for the Fisher
bg: Риба за Рибаря

original: A decent fish.
bg: Добра риба.

original: Here’s a decent fish.
bg: Ето добра риба.

original: Hah... trying to impress me, are you?
bg: Ха... опитваш се да ме впечатлиш, така ли?

original: Anyone can catch a fish in a calm lake.
bg: Всеки може да хване риба в спокойно езеро.

original: Try doing that in the sea.
bg: Опитай да направиш същото в морето.

original: Fine. Can I fish here?
bg: Добре. Мога ли да ловя риба тук?

original: No. This is my spot. Try your luck near the pier.
bg: Не. Това е моето място. Опитай късмета си край кея.

original: Bring me a sea fish and I’ll share an old fisherman’s recipe.
bg: Донеси ми морска риба и ще споделя с теб стара рибарска рецепта.

original: How's the fishing here?
bg: Как е риболовът тук?

original: Not as good as it used to be.
bg: Не е толкова добър, колкото беше преди.

original: You know, there's some good fishing spots outside town.
bg: Знаеш ли, извън града има добри места за риболов.

original: So you’re saying you’re a better fisherman?
bg: Значи казваш, че си по-добър рибар?

original: No, I’m just saying that...
bg: Не, просто казвам, че...

original: Fine then, I challenge you!
bg: Добре тогава, предизвиквам те!

original: Bring me a decent fish from one of your spots...
bg: Донеси ми добра риба от някое от твоите места...

original: And I’ll admit you’re worth something.
bg: И ще призная, че те бива за нещо.

original: A mysterious fish!
bg: Мистериозна риба!

original: It wasn’t easy, but I did it.
bg: Не беше лесно, но успях.

original: Let me see... you actually did it...
bg: Я да видя... наистина си успял...

original: You win... the golden fisherman’s rod is yours.
bg: Печелиш... златната рибарска въдица е твоя.

original: A sea fish.
bg: Морска риба.

original: Here’s a sea fish.
bg: Ето морска риба.

original: Well... I’ll be damned. I guess the recipe is yours... best meal a fisherman can get.
bg: Е, да му се не види. Май рецептата е твоя... най-доброто ястие, което един рибар може да получи.

original: Still, I’m a bit better than you.
bg: И все пак съм малко по-добър от теб.

original: If you really want to beat me, catch a mysterious fish.
bg: Ако наистина искаш да ме победиш, хвани мистериозна риба.

original: Alright, I’ll try.
bg: Добре, ще опитам.

original: Inflation
bg: Инфлация

original: Mercenary rates
bg: Тарифи за наемници

original: We’ll see... I’ll raise my own soldiers... fearless and armed with shiny spears!
bg: Ще видим... Ще си обуча собствени войници... безстрашни и въоръжени с лъскави копия!

original: Alright... alright. Maybe we can discuss a small discount.
bg: Добре... добре. Може би можем да обсъдим малка отстъпка.

original: Why is your service so expensive?
bg: Защо услугите ви са толкова скъпи?

original: Because we’re the only mercenaries around, and there hasn’t been much work lately.
bg: Защото сме единствените наемници наоколо, а напоследък няма много работа.

original: So when someone finally does hire us, we set the price high.
bg: Затова, когато някой най-сетне ни наеме, определяме висока цена.

original: But you just said no one hires you... maybe it’s because of that price.
bg: Но току-що каза, че никой не ви наема... може би заради тази цена.

original: Maybe nobody needs mercenaries... except you.
bg: Може би никой няма нужда от наемници... освен теб.

original: And now that I think about it, maybe every new contract should cost you even more!
bg: А сега като се замисля, може би всеки нов договор трябва да ти струва още повече!

original: That’s ridiculous!
bg: Това е нелепо!

original: Maybe... but what choice do you have?
bg: Може би... но какъв избор имаш?

original: A small discount?
bg: Малка отстъпка?

original: So what kind of discount are we talking about?
bg: И за каква отстъпка говорим?

original: Simple. Bring us some good quality wine. It’s nearly impossible to get these days.
bg: Просто е. Донеси ни хубаво вино. Напоследък е почти невъзможно да се намери.

original: And where exactly am I supposed to find it?
bg: И къде точно трябва да го намеря?

original: No idea... maybe you can make some. Ha ha.
bg: Нямам представа... може би ти можеш да направиш малко. Ха-ха.

original: Give wine.
bg: Дай вино.

original: Here’s some good quality wine.
bg: Ето малко хубаво вино.

original: Mmm... that is good. Where did you get it?
bg: Ммм... това е добро. Откъде го взе?

original: I made it myself.
bg: Направих го сам.

original: Hmm... in that case you can definitely make us some more.
bg: Хмм... в такъв случай със сигурност можеш да ни направиш още.

original: Tell you what... we’ll gladly take your wine as payment instead of money.
bg: Знаеш ли какво... с радост ще приемем виното ти вместо пари.

original: To be honest, we’d only spend the money on wine anyway... just worse wine.
bg: Честно казано, така или иначе щяхме да похарчим парите за вино... само че за по-лошо.

original: I see you're smiling... did you finally get that zombie book?
bg: Виждам, че се усмихваш... най-после ли се сдоби с онази книга за зомбита?

original: Yes... it should have all the answers.
bg: Да... би трябвало да съдържа всички отговори.

original: Good. Now you just need a decent place to raise the dead.
bg: Добре. Сега ти трябва само подходящо място за възкресяване на мъртвите.

original: I expect it’s just like cooking — better ingredients, better results.
bg: Предполагам, че е като при готвенето — по-добри съставки, по-добри резултати.

original: What does cooking have to do with it?
bg: Какво общо има готвенето?

original: Oh, I mean... better corpses make better zombies.
bg: О, искам да кажа... от по-добрите трупове излизат по-добри зомбита.

original: That's quite a disturbing analogy.
bg: Това е доста обезпокоителна аналогия.

original: I told you this is the place!
bg: Казах ти, че това е мястото!

original: And the wires start making all kinds of funny sparks. he he
bg: А жиците започват да хвърлят всякакви смешни искри. Хе-хе.

original: Wait... there’s a lightning storm every <sprite name="day_envy">?
bg: Чакай... всеки <sprite name="day_envy"> ли има гръмотевична буря?

original: Yeah... just like clockwork. This world has become even weirder than I remember.
bg: Да... точно като по часовник. Този свят е станал още по-странен, отколкото го помня.

original: I’m pretty sure that before the apocalypse, zombie resurrection worked perfectly fine without all that elec... whatever.
bg: Почти съм сигурен, че преди апокалипсиса възкресяването на зомбита е работело идеално и без цялото това елек... каквото и да е.

original: Back then the air was full of magic.
bg: По онова време въздухът е бил изпълнен с магия.

original: Shouldn’t we check their notes first?
bg: Не трябва ли първо да проверим записите им?

original: Hmm... looks like blueprints for the equipment they used here.
bg: Хмм... изглеждат като чертежи на оборудването, което са използвали тук.

original: But not a single word about the serum recipe.
bg: Но няма нито дума за рецептата на серума.

original: They keep referring to some book with the formula... the Necronomicon.
bg: Непрекъснато споменават някаква книга с формулата... Некрономикона.

original: Heh... I read that once! Although I only skimmed the cooking section.
bg: Хе-хе... веднъж съм я чел! Макар че само прегледах раздела за готвене.

original: Looks like they took most of the equipment with them...
bg: Изглежда, че са взели по-голямата част от оборудването със себе си...

original: I guess I'll need to find someone who knows more about zombie resurrection... and that book.
bg: Май ще трябва да намеря някого, който знае повече за възкресяването на зомбита... и за тази книга.

original: But look — they left some resurrection serum, and a few notes.
bg: Но виж — оставили са малко серум за възкресение и няколко записки.

original: According to this, they were using electricity to resurrect corpses.
bg: Според това са използвали електричество, за да възкресяват трупове.

original: Using what, sorry?
bg: С какво, моля?

original: See those long thin rope things on the wall? Those are wires... They carry electricity.
bg: Виждаш ли онези дълги тънки неща като въжета по стената? Това са жици... По тях тече електричество.

original: But where would they get electricity here?
bg: Но откъде биха взели електричество тук?

original: Those wire things go all the way up to the top of the tower...
bg: Тези жици стигат чак до върха на кулата...

original: Every <sprite name="day_envy"> when it storms, lightning strikes the tower.
bg: Всеки <sprite name="day_envy"> по време на буря мълния удря кулата.

original: Think you might try resurrecting your own zombies at some point?
bg: Мислиш ли някога да опиташ да възкресяваш собствени зомбита?

original: I bet they were doing it somewhere near the morgue... We need to get into that room.
bg: Обзалагам се, че са го правили някъде край моргата... Трябва да влезем в онази стая.

original: That’s probably where they kept all their resurrection secrets.
bg: Вероятно там са пазели всичките си тайни за възкресението.

original: Yeah... that would be nice. Those green guys are pretty useful.
bg: Да... би било хубаво. Тези зелени типове са доста полезни.

original: I found some notes here about the experiments that the inquisitors were up to.
bg: Тук намерих записки за експериментите, които инквизиторите са правили.

original: They were hoping to resurrect their own zombies, and make them fight the bad ones.
bg: Надявали са се да възкресят свои зомбита и да ги накарат да се бият с лошите.

original: Not a bad idea, actually.
bg: Всъщност не е лоша идея.

original: Looks like they got pretty close, too... They managed to resurrect them. Just couldn’t control them.
